summary: At The University of Tokyo, follow your instructor’s class rule, do not submit AI text or copied answers as your own, keep confidential and unpublished information out of AI tools, and treat contracted services as separate from academic permission.

dimensions.summary: UTokyo leaves AI conditions to individual instructors; students must not present AI-generated text as their own, and copy-paste answers are not accepted as learning. Scope: class and assignment guidance.

do: Follow the instructor’s class or assignment AI rule.
dont: Do not submit AI-generated text or copied answers as your own.

dimensions.summary: UTokyo faculty guidance treats exam questions as highly confidential and says they should not be entered into generative AI tools. Scope: faculty handling of exam questions, not a blanket student exam rule.

do: Treat exam materials as confidential and follow the exam instructions.
dont: Do not infer permission to enter exam questions into AI tools.

dimensions.summary: No source-backed student disclosure rule is included in this candidate; this is not evidence of permission or prohibition.
UTokyo warns students not to input confidential, personal, or unpublished research information and warns faculty not to input exam questions. Scope: student and faculty guidance.

do: Remove confidential, personal, and unpublished information before using an AI tool.
dont: Do not enter confidential data, personal data, unpublished research, or exam questions.

dimensions.summary: UTokyo records Gemini and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat as university-wide contracted AI chat services. Contracted provision does not decide class, assessment, thesis, or research permission.

do: Verify service eligibility and the instructor or project rule.
dont: Do not infer academic permission from a university contract.

dimensions.summary: No source-backed UTokyo research-publication rule is included in this candidate; this is not evidence of permission or prohibition.
